lines.text: The two walk hand in hand.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Commander.
Yeah?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Nothing.
Huh? You can't do that.
Marian lifts the Commander's hand and presses her lips to the back of it.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: You're sweet.
The Commander wraps his arm around Marian's waist and pulls her towards him, burying his face in her neck.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Haha, that tickles.
Mmm... You smell great.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: So do you.
What do I smell like?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Hmm... You've got a very manly smell.
That sounds like a polite way of saying I smell bad.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Not at all. I'd happily smell it for the rest of my life.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Heh... I don't think I'll ever forget this.
Marian kisses the Commander's neck again and again.
H-hold on...

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: What? Come on, just a little more.
No, in front of us.
Marian looks where the Commander is pointing.
A group of deer slowly walks past.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... Whoa.
I've seen animals a few times, but never a whole family like this.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Me neither.
The two of them watch the family of deer in silence for a while.
The deer graze and play with each other, tumbling along the ground.
After a while, they disappear into the undergrowth.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I know the next thing I want to do after our picnic.
Me too.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: What would you like?
A daughter, I think.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Huh? Why?
Because she'd take after you.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Hahaha. That's the same reason I thought a son would be nice.
All right, we'll have two then.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: How far apart?
Hmm... just one year, I'd say.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Hahaha. You're not going to give me a break, huh?
Not a chance.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: They say the first child takes after the father, so the son should be first.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: He'd grow up to be dependable and warm, like a ray of sunlight.
Don't forget kind and gentle.
Because he'd take after his mother.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I'd love that.
Night falls, and the two of them are sitting against a rock sheltered on three sides.
They share a thin blanket, their shoulders pressed together.
Marian.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Yes, Commander?
You had a long day. Get some sleep. I'll take watch.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: You were fighting right alongside me.
I barely did anything apart from just messing around next to you.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Is that what you call sniping a Rapture's core with a pistol from 200 meters out?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Honestly, I can't wait to see what you're capable of when you really try.
Careful. If you fall any harder for me, we might have trouble.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Haha. Let me take watch. Don't push yourself.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I told you, didn't I? I'm a Nikke. I could stay awake for a week without any trouble.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Go ahead and sleep. We've got a long way to go.
But I want to watch you sleep.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Why?
Because you're beautiful when you sleep.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Hahaha. Unfortunately, the answer's still no. It's too dangerous.
We're safe here, and besides, this isn't exactly my first night out in the wild.
Just sleep. You're tired.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I don't know...
Then how about this?
The Commander takes Marian by the shoulder and pulls her toward him.
Marian ends up nestled against his chest.
Now you have no choice but to sleep.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Am I not... heavy?
No, I'd call this a very... comfortable weight. Anyway, it's fine.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: So in other words, I'm heavy.
Not at all.
The Commander strokes Marian's hair.
Marian feels herself relax, and she leans into his shoulder.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Do you know how much is left?
Last time we made it to around 80%, right?
So we've probably got about two days left.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: We're going to make it to the end this time, won't we?
Of course.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I can't wait to have our picnic.
Hmm? What picnic?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: What? Don't pretend like you forgot.
Oh... Yeah. Right. The picnic.
We'll pack a lunch and go to a park with a lake.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I still don't think I could ever go for a military lunch box.
... Look, it may not be much to look at, but you can't beat its practicality.
You know what, I'll go ahead and bring it along. You just need to use it once, and I'm sure you'll like it.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... Haha. Okay. I can't wait.
Yeah. Me too.
Marian nestles deeper into the Commander's arms.
She closes her eyes. He strokes her hair.
That night, neither of them sleeps a wink.
The two crouch down and look at the pack of Raptures beyond the cover.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Given their positioning, we should go with an MC formation.
Yeah. Good call.
... Sorry, I get the formations mixed up sometimes. Is that the one where I provide backup?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... Oh. Yeah, there are a lot of different formations. It's easy to mix them up.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: This one's the one we made using the M from Marian and the C from Commander.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Hehe. It's not really a formation, but just our way of saying we'll figure it out as we go.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: It's more of a joke, really.
Wow, I must be tired, because that didn't even occur to me.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Don't worry about it at all. It happens, especially when you've been fighting as much as we have.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Plus, there's so much we've talked about that it'd be hard to remember every single thing.
Sorry. I'll have to inscribe all of this on my body so I don't forget.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Haha, you shouldn't do that to a perfectly good body.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Just don't ever forget me, okay?
As if I ever could.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Okay, let's go.
Yeah, let's do this.
Marian opens fire.
After hundreds of encounters with Raptures, she can target their cores with ease.
With the minimum number of rounds, she aims only for the cores and lands every shot. One after another, Raptures either fall silent or explode.
The Commander keeps on the move, either drawing their attention or backing Marian up with his pistol.
The Raptures go down fast. The Commander's spirits lift as the battle starts going their way.
Trusting that she feels the same, he turns to look at Marian, who has fought alongside him through so much.
Marian's expression is rigid.
It's a face that shows her mind is somewhere else entirely. And there's something the Commander has learned across dozens of battles.
Accidents always happen at moments like this.
He spots a Rapture off to the side that is taking aim at Marian while she's focused on firing straight ahead.
The Commander runs. The Rapture launches a missile.
Just before the missile lands beside Marian, the Commander pulls her into his arms and rolls.
The explosion shakes the ground, startling Marian. The Commander immediately looks up to locate the Rapture.
The Rapture bursts through the smoke and brings a foreleg crashing down on the two of them.
*Bam!*
Ngh... urk...!
The Commander catches the Rapture's foreleg with his bare hands and holds it back.
His knees buckle and the muscles in his body scream.
Marian, still on her back, raises her machine gun and fires at the Rapture.
The Rapture shudders and shuts down. The Commander quickly falls backwards.
*Huff... huff...!*
Phew...! Are you all right,
Maria-n?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Hehe. Call me Marian, Commander.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Isn't that easier to say?
Oh, yeah. It's definitely...
The Commander freezes.
He stares blankly at Marian.
He stays that way for a long while.
*Smack!*
He punches himself in the face.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Huh...?! Commander!
*Smack!*
He hits himself again. His face begins to swell.
Marian rushes over and grabs his arm.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Commander!
I've lost it. I've actually lost it.
How...? How could I forget you...?!
I've been alive too long. That must be it!
J-just once! If I die just one time, I'll be fine again!

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Commander! Get a hold of yourself!

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: It's okay! It's okay!

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Look at me! Look at my face!
The Commander stares at Marian's face with terror in his eyes.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Remember? My face! My voice! My name! All you need to do is remember!

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: And if you forget, that's okay! I'll keep reminding you!

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: My face! My voice! My name! Remember them again...!

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: It doesn't matter how many times it happens...! Hundreds, thousands, or even more...! I'll keep helping you remember!

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I'll stay right by your side! So it's okay! Don't worry!
Mari...an...

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I won't let you die! And I'll make sure you remember!

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I promise...! To protect you...! No matter what...!
The Commander looks at Marian.
He sees eyes wet with tears, but without a single trace of hesitation in them.
The Commander pulls Marian into his arms.
I'll never forget.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: All right, Commander.
